title: Extrapulmonary TB as a site glossary
dek: Wikipedia splits TB by anatomy: nodes, bone, meninges, miliary. Site names are not specimen instructions and not DST.
story: Wikipedia's extrapulmonary tuberculosis page is a site list: lymph node (historically scrofula), spine (Pott), meninges, pericardium, genitourinary, abdominal, miliary as dissemination. Those names are how clinicians search.

Simplfy already has dedicated clinic plates for meningitis, miliary, pericarditis, pediatric/extrapulmonary diagnosis. This card is the encyclopedia index that should related[] into them rather than re-teach CSF GeneXpert.
HIV shifts the mix toward disseminated and extrapulmonary forms. That is pathogenesis, already on tb-hiv-synergy. The glossary just keeps the site words attached.
deep: A Wikipedia 'lymph node TB' sentence does not tell you to skip NAAT on the node or to treat empirically forever.
Pott disease is vertebral osteomyelitis with a name; imaging and microbiology still required.
Miliary is a radiographic/anatomic pattern of dissemination, with its own plate.
Doses for TBM (higher rifamycin questions, steroids) are WHO objects on tb-meningitis, never here.

visual.caption: Site words Wikipedia will serve, mapped toward existing clinic plates rather than toward a single 'EPTB regimen'.

example.title: Named site, missing specimen
example.setup: Notes say 'Pott disease, start HRZE' with no biopsy/NAAT and no imaging report in the chart.

steps.title: The name is a hypothesis
steps.body: Wikipedia can name vertebral TB; it cannot replace a specimen.

steps.title: Regimen still waits on disease confirmation and DST class

example.takeaway: Anatomy words are an index, not a microbiologic result.
